title: Bond distance is a boundary
claim: Bond distance is a boundary. In a hub-free parity law (knots as vertices of a graph with an unconstrained outside vertex; seams as edges, open ends as edges to the outside): (1) the bond distance between two distinctions is the least boundary, counting seams and the open ends held inside, of a connected set of knots whose outside is connected and which has both on its boundary, minus one; (2) a set of knots holding no open end and joined to the rest by one seam pins that seam and splits the allowed states, so no knot crosses it: closing every open end of a region seals it off; two seams tie but do not decouple; (3) every such two-sided boundary of at least three distinctions is a knot, so a long region with a short boundary is a shortcut and closed strips collapse; (4) growing only at knots that hold two or more open ends grows exactly the two-way thread, whose bond distance is the number of knots on the path plus one: a native logical number line.
failure_conditions: A pair whose least knot differs from the least boundary of a connected region with connected outside containing both on its boundary.
A one-seam region without open ends whose seam is not pinned, or a knot crossing it.
A connected region with connected outside and boundary of size >= 3 whose boundary is not a knot.
A run of the two-open-ends rule that is not a path with one open end per inner knot, or whose bond distances differ from path knots + 1.
foundation_claim_scope: Finite hub-free parity laws and the two-open-ends growth rule; bond distance as in NATIVE-NETWORK-20261021-001.

validation.independence: Written by Claude in one session at the repository owner's request on 2026-11-07.
validation.status: prose proofs; check.py runs five checks with rejected controls (240 exhaustive pairs, 31 sealed clusters, 46 regions and a 31-bead strip, 42 runs of the rule); no human or external review
validation.novelty: known-overlap-found: bonds as circuits of the cocycle matroid and bridge arguments are classical (Whitney; Oxley); the delta is the reading for growth at open ends (sealing freezes, short boundaries collapse, the two-open-ends rule grows the number line).
